qualifying_findings.title: Continue CLI unattended and auto modes rely on incomplete destructive-command denylist
qualifying_findings.summary: NVD records a high-severity Continue CLI vulnerability where unattended/headless execution grants Bash allow permission and blocks only commands recognized by an incomplete destructive-command evaluator, allowing crafted command forms to bypass the intended barrier.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Continue CLI headless mode and auto mode; NVD CVSS 3.1 HIGH 7.4; CWE-184.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Coding agents that can run shell commands need approval boundaries that fail closed and parse commands structurally rather than depending on incomplete denylist matching.

upstream_routing.note: General Continue CLI developer-tool background routes upstream; local coverage should focus on destructive-command approval controls.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High for NVD publication and vulnerability class; affected fixed version should be rechecked from the upstream advisory during ingest.
follow_up_actions: Consider a local leaf for unattended coding-agent command authorization bypass.
Check whether existing coding-agent command approval boundary coverage should link this CVE.

qualifying_findings.title: PraisonAI advisory cluster exposes agent SSRF, missing auth, approval bypass, and MCP origin validation flaws

visible_dates.github_advisory_dates_note: GitHub advisories fetched through the GitHub API showed June 2026 publication/update dates for at least GHSA-5r34-2g38-6569; this finding qualifies on the NVD in-window publication dates.

qualifying_findings.summary: NVD published several PraisonAI records on August 25. The records cover redirect-following SSRF in `web_crawl`, missing authentication in AgentServer and served agent endpoints even when tokens/API keys are configured, an agent-controlled file rewrite path missing a required approval decorator, and MCP HTTP Stream origin validation that accepts attacker-controlled `localhost.attacker.com` origins.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: PraisonAI and praisonaiagents before fixed releases including praisonaiagents 1.6.58 and praisonai 4.6.58; NVD severities include HIGH 7.5, HIGH 8.2, MEDIUM 6.1, HIGH 7.6, and HIGH 8.8.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: The cluster spans all major agent control-plane boundaries: web retrieval trust, network invocation authentication, mutation-tool approval, and browser-to-localhost/MCP request origin checks.

upstream_routing.note: Broad PraisonAI product/framework background belongs upstream.
General multi-agent framework selection and coding-agent workflows route upstream.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High for NVD publication and vulnerability summaries. GitHub advisory pages may show earlier advisory publication dates, so ingest should distinguish newly indexed NVD records from original disclosure timing.
follow_up_actions: Split into focused local leaves if ingest needs separate SSRF, missing-auth, approval-bypass, and MCP-origin pages.

qualifying_findings.title: browse-mcp browser tools allow caller-controlled filesystem paths before 0.8.2

visible_dates.upstream_release_note: Release/changelog reference points to 0.8.2 dated 2026-06-13; this finding qualifies on NVD in-window publication.

qualifying_findings.summary: NVD records browse-mcp before 0.8.2 as allowing MCP-capable agents to use caller-controlled paths in browser download/save/load state operations, creating host filesystem read/write boundary risk for a Playwright-based browser MCP server.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: browse-mcp before 0.8.2; Playwright-based headless browser MCP filesystem boundary.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Browser agents often handle untrusted web content and local state. Caller-controlled save/load paths can turn browser automation into host filesystem compromise or persistence.

upstream_routing.note: Broad browse-mcp/MCP server catalog context routes upstream.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: Medium-high. NVD details are sufficient for raw intake, but ingest should confirm exact CVSS/CWE details because the first NVD query output was keyword-filtered and concise.
follow_up_actions: Check local browser MCP and filesystem containment leaves for linkage.
Confirm whether the release note date means this is a newly indexed old advisory.

qualifying_findings.title: mcp-shell default deployment permits unrestricted shell execution before 0.6.0
qualifying_findings.summary: NVD records mcp-shell before 0.6.0 as starting the documented bare-binary deployment without a security policy when `MCP_SHELL_SEC_CONFIG_FILE` is unset. The command validator short-circuits when security is disabled, allowing arbitrary commands supplied to the `shell_exec` MCP tool.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: mcp-shell before 0.6.0; NVD CVSS 4.0 HIGH 8.6; CWE-78.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: A shell-capable MCP server must be secure by default. Opt-in policy with unrestricted default execution breaks least privilege for local agents connected over stdio.

upstream_routing.note: MCP server catalog background routes upstream; local page should preserve the security-default and shell-execution boundary.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High for NVD and GitHub advisory substance; disclosure timing caveat because GitHub advisory is older than the collection window.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, decide whether this extends existing coding-agent command approval boundary coverage or needs a separate mcp-shell leaf.
Preserve the secure-by-default lesson for MCP tool servers.

qualifying_findings.title: Nextcloud MCP Server accepts unauthenticated vector webhooks when secret is unset
qualifying_findings.summary: NVD records Nextcloud MCP Server before 0.117.2 as leaving `POST /webhooks/nextcloud` unauthenticated by default because `WEBHOOK_SECRET` defaults to null and startup does not require it. Attackers can spoof user IDs in webhook payloads and delete or corrupt vector embeddings in Qdrant.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: nextcloud-mcp-server before 0.117.2; vector sync webhook and Qdrant embedding store.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: MCP data synchronization endpoints need authenticated event provenance. An unauthenticated webhook can corrupt retrieval indexes and cross user data boundaries.

upstream_routing.note: Broad Nextcloud MCP Server catalog facts route upstream.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High for vulnerability summary and affected versions; original GitHub advisory predates the cutoff, so this is best treated as an in-window NVD publication of an older advisory.
follow_up_actions: Check whether local MCP data movement and final-query authorization pages should reference authenticated webhook provenance.
Verify fixed release details before ingest.

qualifying_findings.title: QWED LLM verification API allows authenticated RCE through unsafe SymPy parsing before 5.1.2
qualifying_findings.summary: NVD and the GitHub advisory describe QWED verification infrastructure before 5.1.2 passing tenant-controlled math expressions to SymPy `parse_expr()` without restricted namespaces. Because default signup/API-key issuance allows ordinary tenant access, attackers can execute arbitrary Python code in the API server process.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: qwed package version 5.1.1 / qwed-verification before 5.1.2; `POST /verify/math` and batch math verification paths; NVD CVSS 3.1 HIGH 8.8; CWE-94.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Security/evaluation infrastructure becomes part of the AI release gate. If verification endpoints execute code from untrusted input, the assurance control plane itself becomes a compromise path.

upstream_routing.note: General deterministic verification practice routes upstream; local coverage should focus on verification control-plane security.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High for vulnerability mechanics and patched version; timing should be recorded as in-window NVD publication of an older GitHub advisory.
